newsitem.title: USA: Rubin repeats balanced budget amendment opposition.
newsitem.headline: Rubin repeats balanced budget amendment opposition.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said Monday that a balanced budget amendment to the Constitution is a threat to U.S. economic health, would expose the economy to unacceptable risks and should not be adopted.

In prepared testimony before the House Judiciary Committee, Rubin also said that he believed an agreement on a balanced budget could be achieved this year and added that a country that ignores its fiscal responsibility does so at the peril that it will be punished with higher interest rates by global markets.
"The sum total is that politically, historically and economically the forces are in place to balance the budget," he said. "We are not far apart. Now we need to get the job done."

Rubin, in opposing the legislation to amend the Constitution, said that there was a new atmosphere in Washington as well as an enforcing factor through financial markets on policy makers to maintain fiscal responsibility.
"A nation that does not address fiscal matters will be severely punished by markets with high interest rates that could impair or even severely impair its economy," he said.
Rubin added that for these reasons and others, "I believe that we can put in place balanced budget legislation this year."
